_comment: Reviewed interior-carbon locant crosswalks between the pinned reference parser's
numbering and the P-25.3.3.3 numbering this engine emits. Frozen deliberately: the
correspondence is reviewed once and pinned, never rediscovered and accepted at test time.
Each record carries BOTH graphs and the crosswalk between them. A crosswalk is admissible
only if it is bijective, preserves every element and every edge, leaves every peripheral
label pointwise fixed, and carries the parser graph exactly onto the IUPAC graph.
Every conversion also carries a certificate computed from the parser graph and its fixed
perimeter alone - never from the engine's own choice of anchor. P-25.3.3.3.1-2 takes the
nearest peripheral atom and, among equally near ones, the lowest locant, with the bond
distance as a superscript. Graph correspondence says WHICH atom; the certificate says the
label is the one the rule requires. Pyrene is the published control (FR-5.5.2 prints
10b -> 3a(1) and 10c -> 5a(1)); the test also keeps a negative control that must fail.

systems.parser_graph_note: the parser cannot read this citation's interior indicated hydrogen, so the skeleton was taken from the hydrogen-free citation; it establishes connectivity and numbering only, never the hydrogen state
